title: Altitude Alert and Warning Systems
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part II Ch 7

1.q: How does a radio altimeter work?
o: Measures the Doppler shift of a CW transmission.
Measures the Doppler shift of a pulse transmission.
Measures the time from transmission to the reception of a CW frequency.

2.q: Radio altimeter gives height indications by:
o: Measuring the Doppler frequency shift in transmitted frequency.
Measuring time diff. of a CW transmitted at fixed frequency.
Measuring time diff. of a CW transmitted at changing frequency.

3.q: In case landing gears are retracted, radio altimeter is showing
o: More then actual clearance.
Less than actual clearance.
Actual clearance.

4.q: In case landing gears are retracted, radio altimeter
o: Under- reads
Over - reads
Reads - correct

5.q: The radio altimeter indicates 2000 ft. What is the minimum height that the aircraft would be at?
o: 1935' in cruising configuration
1935' in landing configuration
1945' in landing configuration

6.q: During the approach, a crew reads on the radio altimeter the value of 650 ft. This is an indication of the true?
o: Height of the lowest wheels with regard to the ground at any time.
Height of the aircraft with regard to the ground at any time.
Height of the aircraft with regard to the runway.

7.q: For most radio altimeters, when a system error occurs during approach the?
o: Height indication is removed.
OH lamp flashes red and the audio signal sounds.
DH lamp flashes red.

8.q: A radio altimeter can be defined as a?
o: Ground radio aid used to measure the true height of the aircraft.
Ground radio aid used to measure the true altitude of the aircraft.
Self-contained on-board aid used to measure the true height of the aircraft

9.q: The data supplied by a radio altimeter?
o: Indicates the distance between the ground and the aircraft.
Concerns only the decision height.
Is used only by the radio altimeter indicator.

10.q: The low-altitude radio altimeters used in precision approaches: 1. operate in the 1540–1660 MHz range 2. are of the pulsed type 3. are of the frequency-modulation type 4. have an operating range of 0 to 5000 ft 5. have a precision of ±2 ft between 0 and 500 ft. The combination of correct statements is:

11.q: The operating frequency range of a low altitude radio altimeter is?
o: 2700 MHz to 2900 MHz.
5 GHz.
4200 MHz to 4400 MHz.

12.q: Modern low altitude radio altimeters emit waves in the following frequency band?
o: HF (High Frequency).
UHF (Ultra High Frequency).
SHF (Super High Frequency).

13.q: The operation of the radio altimeter of a modern aircraft is based on?
o: Pulse modulation of the carrier wave.
A combination of frequency modulation and pulse modulation.
Frequency modulation of the carrier wave.

14.q: In low altitude radio altimeters height measurement (above ground) is based upon?
o: A triangular amplitude modulation wave, for which modulation phase shift between transmitted and received waves after ground reflection is measured.
A frequency modulation wave, for which the frequency variation between the transmitted wave and the received wave after ground reflection is measured.
A pulse transmission, for which time between transmission and reception is measured on a circular scanning screen.

15.q: The aircraft radio equipment which emits on a frequency of 4400 MHz is the?
o: Weather radar.
Primary radar.
Radio altimeter.
Aircraft based and indicates true altitude.
Aircraft based and indicates pressure altitude.
Aircraft based and indicates true height.
Crucial to GPWS operations.
Not required for GPWS operations.
Used to determine altitude above msl.

18.q: For the landing configuration a radio altimeter indicates?
o: Height of the aircraft above the ground.
Height of the flight deck above the ground.
Height of the main wheel above the ground.

19.q: Low altitude radio altimeters operate on the  wavelength?
o: Metric.
Decimetric.
Centimetric.

20.q: If there is a fault in the system the radalt display will?
o: Needle will disappear and an alarm flag will appear, possibly accompanied by an audio warning.
Freeze.
Turn red and activate an aural warning.
True Altitude.
Pressure altitude.
Height above the ground or water over which the aircraft is flying.
Height above terrain.
Pressure altitude.
Density altitude.

23.q: The failure of the radio altimeter would cause?
o: Loss of pressure altitude data.
Loss of density altitude data.
Loss of height data.

24.q: A radio altimeter has a maximum effective height because?
o: At greater heights the signal will be too weak.
At greater heights signal from different modulation cycles will overlap.
At greater heights the signal will be absorbed by moisture in the air.

25.q: Radio altimeters are accurate only within the height range?
o: Zero to 50 ft.
Zero to 500 ft.
Zero ft to 2500 ft.

26.q: If the GPWS activates, and alerts the pilot with an aural warning DON'T SINK (two times), it is because:
o: during take-off or missed approach manoeuvre, the aircraft has started to lose altitude.
during landing the aircraft is below Glide Path.
during landing if landing gear is unsafe.

27.q: The GPWS (Ground Proximity Warning System) is active for a height range from:
o: 0 ft to 2500 ft measured by the radio altimeter
50 ft to 2500 ft measured by the radio altimeter
50 ft to 1500 ft measured by the radio altimeter

28.q: Can an RA be generated against an aircraft that is not ACAS Il equipped?
o: An RA can be generated against all aircraft equipped with an altitude reporting transponder (Mode S or Mode A/C).
An RA can be generated against all aircraft equipped with a transponder (Mode A).
An RA can be generated against all aircraft equipped with no transponder onboard.
TA
Cautionary RA
Preventive RA

ex.1: Book note: a Doppler shift needs relative motion, so a radio altimeter does not use one.
ex.4: Book note: the radio altimeter is calibrated with the landing gear down.
